l_toll_faces.label: Faces on the cards
l_toll_faces.text: Every toll card carries a printed likeness, and the Guild sends copies south with its forecasts to whoever pays.

l_outriders_asking.label: Outriders asking
l_outriders_asking.text: Four days before he reached Knock, Guild outriders rode north from the Tollhouse asking after an old man, wounded and masked.

l_corin_outrider.label: Corin rode with them
l_corin_outrider.text: Corin Asch rode with Guild outriders twenty years ago, and knows Brannick Hale by sight.

l_hatch_value.label: The bale's value
l_hatch_value.text: MOTHER valued Knock's wool at four units this week and five last month, for the same wool.

l_larkspur.label: "Larkspur"
l_larkspur.text: With his last breath, under the wind, the stranger said a word: Larkspur.

l_walked_west.label: Walked west
l_walked_west.text: The stranger walked a long way west on a bad wound, into the afternoon sun.

l_sealed_wound.label: Machine-sealed wound
l_sealed_wound.text: His old wound was sealed by a machine, not stitched — real hospital work.

l_burned_mark.label: Burned-off mark
l_burned_mark.text: He deliberately burned a printed mark off his forearm.

l_crate_print.label: Crate print
l_crate_print.text: The marks at the burn's edge match the print on MOTHER's old crates.

l_record_hand.label: Record shorthand
l_record_hand.text: His notebook is written in the same shorthand as the Cistern's records.

l_sigil.label: Half-sun sign
l_sigil.text: His dust mask carries a painted sign: half a sun with no ground, or an open hand.

l_photo_light.label: Wrong shadows
l_photo_light.text: In the photograph the shadows on your face and on the towers fall different ways.

l_photo_grain.label: No grain
l_photo_grain.text: The photograph has no grain at all. The dust in it is drawn, not caught.

l_mother_city.label: "There is no city"
l_mother_city.text: Asked whether the stranger came from a city, MOTHER said there is no city — and said it like a thing decided.

l_mother_sealed.label: Outbound entries
l_mother_sealed.text: MOTHER's log holds three sealed entries marked OUTBOUND, years apart, each saying "population variance unchanged".

l_pressure.label: Constant pressure
l_pressure.text: The reservoir pressure has not changed in years. Reservoirs drop. This one is being fed.

l_archive_label.label: Return on relocation
l_archive_label.text: The Archive door is stencilled CONTINUITY RECORDS — RETURN ON RELOCATION.

l_teo_held.label: Teo held
l_teo_held.text: Mags's partner Teo Marsh is held by the Rust Dogs under the overpass for a debt.

l_stranger_shale.label: Through Shale
l_stranger_shale.text: The old stranger passed through Shale three weeks ago, bought water with a ring, and asked for the overpass.

l_pumps_remote.label: Pumps driven remotely
l_pumps_remote.text: Shale's pumps have no working switch; they are driven from somewhere north along the pipe.

l_pumps_clock.label: The water clock
l_pumps_clock.text: The pumps run at fixed hours that changed once for two months, as if someone far away turned a dial.

l_pump_manual.label: Pump manual
l_pump_manual.text: Dov Reese has the pumps' manual; half of it is in a print nobody in Shale can read.

l_pump_manual_hand.label: Manual in city print
l_pump_manual_hand.text: The unreadable half of the pump manual is the same print as MOTHER's crates: SUPPLY — NETWORK 4.

l_pressure_shale.label: Shale's pressure
l_pressure_shale.text: Shale's pump pressure is as constant as the Cistern's. Both are fed from the same somewhere.

l_seed_buyer.label: Seed at any price
l_seed_buyer.text: Factor Pike buys viable seed at absurd prices, in advance, for a client he will not name.

l_mags_buyout.label: Who owns the Dry Well
l_mags_buyout.text: On paper the Dry Well saloon is Factor Pike's: a guild loan against the deed, and a signed buyout Mags is hiding from the town.

l_futures.label: Paper futures
l_futures.text: The Exchange at Ninebridge sells sealed sheets that say what will happen, where, and when. Buyers pay more for the seal unbroken.

l_exchange_paid.label: Paid from the floor
l_exchange_paid.text: The outriders who shot the stranger were paid from the Exchange: two riders, four days, "westbound traveller, confirmed", by order of the floor.

l_packet_water.label: The packet was water
l_packet_water.text: The sealed packet you carried east was a schedule: SHALE — 0.62 — and a date. Somebody at the Exchange buys Shale's water by the number.

l_sable.label: Lot four is a Calloway
l_sable.text: The young woman on the auction block is Sable Calloway, nineteen, fifty-eight Tolls in debt. Wren had a sister.

l_strike_forecast.label: The strike is forecast
l_strike_forecast.text: The guild holds a sealed sheet saying the porters' stoppage ends on the third day with nothing won. It was written before the strike began.

l_odile_hand.label: Odile knows the hand
l_odile_hand.text: Odile Marchetti recognised the notation on the stranger's map at a glance: the Exchange's own, from before she left it.

l_well_powder.label: Something in the well
l_well_powder.text: The north trough at Openfield carries a bitter salt the south trough does not. The well is being dosed, not blighted.

l_tobias_nights.label: Tobias at the well
l_tobias_nights.text: The Elder's son goes to the well after midnight with a lantern and a pouch, and comes back without the pouch.

l_openfield_sheet.label: Openfield burns
l_openfield_sheet.text: A guild forecast says Openfield burns in the Long Night if its harvest rises above plan. Someone here has read it until it fell apart.

l_seed_corso.label: The guild buys seed by night
l_seed_corso.text: Daichi Nakai, the Tollmen's hand on the lane, pays a yard hand in Tolls for a crate of Choir seed every night — for Factor Pike's unnamed client.

l_stranger_unwritten.label: He was one of theirs
l_stranger_unwritten.text: The stranger who died at your door was Hollis Dray of the Unwritten: the Choir's hidden circle, who keep no likeness and sign nothing.

l_unwritten_kill.label: Some of them kill
l_unwritten_kill.text: Petra Mason said it plainly: some of the Unwritten break a forecast by killing the person it is about.

l_sump_one_purse.label: Two clans, one purse
l_sump_one_purse.text: Both Sump clans are paid by the fourth day from the same guild purse, to clear the same tunnel toward the same door. Factor Pike wants what is behind it.

l_c4_order.label: Relocate on schedule
l_c4_order.text: Cistern 4 was ordered by the city to send its people to the Precinct on a date. Its door failed; its water was cut for not complying. The order carries the Ledger's seal.

l_c4_same_order.label: The same order
l_c4_same_order.text: The city sent Cistern 4 the order MOTHER's sealed OUTBOUND entries answer: relocate. Cistern 4 could not. Cistern 9 would not.

l_c4_diary.label: To whoever comes
l_c4_diary.text: The last doctor of Cistern 4 wrote a letter to the city that never came. It is in your pack. The city is east.

l_face_flagged.label: Your face is on file
l_face_flagged.text: The gate's scanner knew your face before you gave a name: a file, a number, and a status the clerk had never seen — ADMIT ON SIGHT.

l_fines_forecast.label: Fined in advance
l_fines_forecast.text: The Precinct has fined you for three offences you have not committed yet. Each carries a forecast date.

l_nine_log.label: The assessor's private log
l_nine_log.text: Assessor Nine keeps an unlawful record of every forecast that failed. It would like to know where the errors come from.

l_precinct_rationing.label: Point eight
l_precinct_rationing.text: The Precinct's water is rationed to point eight of its number since the Sallow's pumps changed. The Plan rebalances.

l_cisterns_relocate.label: Reserves on schedule
l_cisterns_relocate.text: The records office lists the continuity reserves by number with a relocation date against each. Nine's says: OUTSTANDING.

l_kiosk_wire.label: The kiosk's wire
l_kiosk_wire.text: The talking kiosk in Old Market is spliced to the Precinct's lamp wire. Whatever it says about a face, it is reading off the city's file.

l_broker_two.label: The hatch has two voices
l_broker_two.text: The Broker's voice box speaks in one voice, but the hand that takes the coin changes size between morning and night.

l_market_ration.label: Point six
l_market_ration.text: The Precinct's ration is point eight. Old Market's standpipe is turned to point six. The difference goes somewhere.

l_sigil_shale.label: Sign at the mission
l_sigil_shale.text: The stranger's half-sun sign is painted on the Choir tent-pole in Shale.

l_larkspur_calla.label: Calla knew the word
l_larkspur_calla.text: Sister Calla knew the dead man's word, and said a man at Openfield would know more.

l_hollis_city.label: The boards
l_hollis_city.text: Hollis Crane lived in a city with screens that showed who paid, who owed, and who was next.

l_ring_shale.label: The ring
l_ring_shale.text: The stranger's ring, bought back from Pardo: two letters and a half-sun inside the band.

l_ines_burned.label: Burned letter
l_ines_burned.text: Ines burned your letter about the city and would not say why.

l_map_traded.label: The map for water
l_map_traded.text: He carried a folded map with names on it, and meant to trade it to Kessler for water.

l_outriders.label: The outriders
l_outriders.text: The guild's two outriders ride the highway west past Shale, and nobody at Tollhouse 9 will say what they did three weeks ago.

l_pike_paid.label: Paid, as per
l_pike_paid.text: The Tollhouse 9 ledger: two outriders paid eighty Tolls for "one traveller, westbound, confirmed" — as per Factor Pike, post nine-west.

l_outriders_confessed.label: A contract, not a man
l_outriders_confessed.text: Cass Mohr admitted it: a road contract from Pike's post, confirmed and paid. "He walked off it."

l_signal_mast.label: The hill with the mast
l_signal_mast.text: Signal Hill, east along the highway: a mast, a dead station, a voice that talks to itself. The guild will not go up there.

l_fence_night.label: Chain-link at the wall's end
l_fence_night.text: The guild finished its wall with chain-link and wire. The tower lamp sweeps it every minute or so.

l_packet.label: The sealed packet
l_packet.text: A guild packet for the Exchange at Ninebridge, nine days, unopened. Breaking the seal makes the bearer owe a sum not written on the outside.

l_terminal_record.label: A courier on record
l_terminal_record.text: The gate terminal stamped you through as a guild courier. The record went somewhere east.

l_bikes_salt.label: Salt in the tread
l_bikes_salt.text: The outriders' tyres carry salt-pan salt. The salt pan is the road the stranger took to Shale.

l_nikko_word.label: One word, westward
l_nikko_word.text: Nikko Bracco heard the stranger say one word as he lay on the salt — past them, west, toward the salt cut.

l_drywells_station.label: The station answers
l_drywells_station.text: Oren Tulley, who fixes pumps: the Dry Wells station "answers to somebody". Everything with a pipe in it does.

l_raid_plan.label: Vasha's plan
l_raid_plan.text: Vasha and four Dogs will wait in the salt by Tollhouse 9. You start it at the gate; they finish it.

l_pass_hands.label: Hands, not paper
l_pass_hands.text: A forged pass passes on how you hold it. The sergeant looks at hands.

l_relay_city.label: The relay answers
l_relay_city.text: Signal Hill's relay is still linked to something east that acknowledges it. Ninety years on, it is part of something alive.

l_relay_west_line.label: A line west
l_relay_west_line.text: The relay feeds a nightly bulletin down a second line, west into the Sallow, to a pump station marked DW-4.

l_relay_denied.label: DENIED
l_relay_denied.text: Three weeks ago someone at Signal Hill asked upstream for the bulletin to stop. The answer was one word.

l_relay_grid.label: Something filed you
l_relay_grid.text: Through the grid link, the relay's upstream read your serial, your position and the hour, and filed them.

l_relay_name.label: A name upstream
l_relay_name.text: You typed a name into Signal Hill's relay and something east acknowledged it. A second lamp came on and stayed on.

l_broadcast_kessler.label: The second name
l_broadcast_kessler.text: The voice at Signal Hill reads the stranger's list: the overpass, Kessler, day forty-five, killed by Kade's hand.

l_voice_restarted.label: Started again
l_voice_restarted.text: The voice at Signal Hill started again three weeks ago, the night an old man came down from the station.

l_stranger_signal.label: He slept at the station
l_stranger_signal.text: The stranger spent a day at Signal Hill's station and scratched the half-sun and a tally of twenty-six days into the cot frame.

l_dw_bypass.label: The family tap
l_dw_bypass.text: A hand-made branch off the Dry Wells line feeds the shacks. Whatever Shale gets, the Marrs take a little first.

l_dw_ghosts.label: Ghosts of a cistern
l_dw_ghosts.text: The Marrs walked out of another cistern, east, with a number on it, when its pumps stopped and its door did not open.

l_dw_schedule.label: Shale at 0.62
l_dw_schedule.text: The Dry Wells console holds Shale at 0.62 on a schedule changed from upstream: six, eleven, four, nine. The last change cut Shale, and it was not the drought.

l_dw_target.label: A number, not a measure
l_dw_target.text: 0.62 is not an amount of water. The schedule is written to hold Shale at a target.

l_dw_log_hand.label: The log in record hand
l_dw_log_hand.text: The console's change log is written and signed in the same record shorthand as the Cistern's outbound logs.

l_dw_diary.label: The pump man's last entry
l_dw_diary.text: "Shale cut to .62. Not drought. Told no one. Who would I tell."

l_dw_halfmoon.label: The old half-moon
l_dw_halfmoon.text: The lead seal on the Dry Wells governor carries the Tollmen's half-moon, pressed long before there were Tollmen.

l_c9_fed.label: C9 RESERVE — HELD
l_c9_fed.text: The Cistern is on the Dry Wells schedule: a tank on a line, its pressure held constant from outside.

l_kite_seen.label: A kite
l_kite_seen.text: Something crossed the sun with no bird in it: long wings, no beat, and it looked at you.

l_kite_on_the_pan.label: A kite came down
l_kite_on_the_pan.text: A kite came down on the white pan south of the track and sat for two days. Where it sat there is a truck now.

l_drifter_owes.label: Ignacio Amory owes you
l_drifter_owes.text: The drifter whose leg you saved will be in Shale, or at the overpass, and says he owes you a thing he cannot name yet.

l_wheel_passing.label: The Wheel is in the Sallow
l_wheel_passing.text: A rider of the Wheel at a trough that should be dry: the nomads are somewhere east this month.

l_wheel_where.label: Where the Wheel camps
l_wheel_where.text: East of the dead windpumps, in the lee of the hill, a week at a time. Cart ruts and horse dung on the pan.

l_walker_mark.label: The walker's hand
l_walker_mark.text: The man walking east at night had a mark burned off the back of his hand, the way the stranger's was.

l_walker_east.label: Walking east to a number
l_walker_east.text: A man walking east with no water said something read him his name, then east, then a number where he stops.

l_walker_warning.label: "Don't let it read yours"
l_walker_warning.text: The walker, with water in him, looked at you afraid and said: don't let it read yours.

l_windpumps_locked.label: Brakes set from away
l_windpumps_locked.text: The windpumps were not broken; their brakes were set, all six, the same day, from somewhere else.

l_windpumps_network.label: Field 2, Network 4
l_windpumps_network.text: The windpumps' brake cable runs east along the pipe toward Dry Wells: the same network that sets Shale's water switched this field off.

l_copper_east.label: Copper goes east
l_copper_east.text: Coil copper from the dead pumps goes to a man at Tollhouse 9 who does not write it down, and east of him. Someone is winding motors.

l_orchard_thieves.label: Green fruit, a Dog's plate
l_orchard_thieves.text: Whoever robs the Choir's orchard takes only the green fruit and dropped a Rust Dog's child-sized plate in the wall.

l_orchard_well.label: The orchard's own water
l_orchard_well.text: The orchard well tastes of stone, not pipe: the one water near Shale that is not on the network.

l_wreck_skid.label: A truck stopped like a toy
l_wreck_skid.text: The convoy truck on the pan was running flat out in a straight line and was stopped dead. No crew; drag marks toward the ring.

l_hound_dormant.label: The thing in the ring
l_hound_dormant.text: A four-legged machine sits in a ring of fused salt beside the wreck. Not rusting. A light deep in its lens.

l_hound_make.label: A crown over a gear
l_hound_make.text: The machine's maker's mark: a crown over a gear. Pre-Burn, and not the city's work.

l_hound_controller.label: The slab wakes it
l_hound_controller.text: The grey slab from the cab warms when the machine's lens sees it, and the machine listens through it.

l_hound_in_shale.label: A machine in the yard
l_hound_in_shale.text: The machine from the pan sits in the sheriff's yard and looks at everything that comes in at night.

l_windpumps.label: A line of windpumps
l_windpumps.text: From the top of Signal Hill: a line of dead windpumps to the south-east, where nothing on the map says anything is.

l_jonah_tower.label: Forty feet of rungs
l_jonah_tower.text: Dov sends Jonah up the windpump tower every week for the bent vane. Half the rungs are gone.

l_jonah_patrol.label: Alone on the east street
l_jonah_patrol.text: Jonah walks the east street alone from midnight to four. The four rifles that shoot are asleep.

l_jonah_water.label: The deputy drinks last
l_jonah_water.text: The east cistern has gone green. By the ration, the deputy drinks from it last.

l_ilya.label: The man behind the yard
l_ilya.text: Ilya Strand, who was the militia's best shot, drinks behind the yard and counts their misses.

l_ilya_raid.label: The wind was right
l_ilya_raid.text: Ilya was three nights east on a hunt when the Dogs raided Shale; Vasha Kade led it. He has never said what he lost.

l_ada_protection.label: A rate card
l_ada_protection.text: After the deputy died, Pike came to the sheriff with a rate card for guild protection, and she did not throw him out.

l_forecast_broken.label: The list was wrong
l_forecast_broken.text: Jonah Reese lived past the thirtieth day. If the list is a forecast, it has been broken once.

l_hollis_knew_mask.label: Hollis knew the sign
l_hollis_knew_mask.text: Hollis Crane recognised the half-sun sign from a man he knew forty years ago, in the city.

l_pike_reported.label: Pike reported him
l_pike_reported.text: Factor Pike reported the stranger's conversation to the Tollmen post east, as per.

l_tracks_overpass.label: Tracks to the highway
l_tracks_overpass.text: His tracks leave Shale north-west, toward the dead highway, alone.

l_kessler_stranger.label: "Tell the bunker"
l_kessler_stranger.text: The stranger's last words to Kessler were "tell the bunker" — he knew where he was going, and that it was ours.

l_wren_found.label: Shot by paid men
l_wren_found.text: Wren found him: he said he was shot by people who were paid to shoot him, and would rather give the paper to a thief than a bank.

l_city_counts.label: The city counts us
l_city_counts.text: The stranger told Perpetua the city counts everyone out here, keeps a list with dates, and that the paper is the list.

l_wren_page.label: Torn page
l_wren_page.text: Wren kept a page the stranger dropped while burning his notebook. Same cipher.

l_name_jonah.label: Jonah Reese — within the month
l_name_jonah.text: The first name on the map: Jonah Reese, Shale, within the month of the day the stranger died.

l_name_vey.label: Ada Vey — four months
l_name_vey.text: The second name Hollis read: Ada Vey, Shale, four months.

l_name_vey_partial.label: V-E-Y-A
l_name_vey_partial.text: The second block on the map half-read: V, E, Y, A. Someone else in Shale.

l_pike_saw_map.label: Pike saw the map
l_pike_saw_map.text: Factor Pike has seen the stranger's map in your hands and sold you the key to it. The Tollmen will know by the next caravan.

l_ring_gone.label: Missing ring
l_ring_gone.text: The stranger had worn a ring until shortly before he died. He traded or lost it near the end.

l_pumps_schedule.label: The relief schedule
l_pumps_schedule.text: The Sink's three relief pumps run to a Precinct schedule, and in spring two of them are turned to the Precinct's supply, as per Plan. The line on the pier rises a hand a year since.

l_sink_numbers.label: The drowned's numbers
l_sink_numbers.text: The tally wall in the Sink keeps the citizen numbers of the drowned beside their names, and somebody sells the numbers up the stair every spring.

l_sato_numbers.label: A dead woman's card
l_sato_numbers.text: Sato's forged cards carry the numbers of people who died in the Sink; he says the Sink gives him a few every spring.

l_pale_harvest.label: What the cold box holds
l_pale_harvest.text: Teng's cold box fills from the Pale's store, and the Pale take from people who owe them, who walk back off the east bank lighter.

l_rev_spire.label: Ninety-one landings
l_rev_spire.text: In the reel the stranger came down a stair of ninety-odd landings lit with the city's own tubes. One house in Meridian has that many floors above a stair.

l_rev_bundle.label: Twelve faces
l_rev_bundle.text: He carried a bundle of photographs with cipher under each, and a sheet of twelve lines in the same cipher. The fourth face was yours, older.

l_rev_gate.label: A rider at the gate
l_rev_gate.text: At dawn a guild rider waited on the road west of the Wall with a brand on the saddle you have seen at Tollhouse 9. The stranger saw the rider waiting, and went west anyway.

l_st_tank.label: Live at two
l_st_tank.text: Block Seven's main is live only at night, and the lifts' three-minute check at two draws the whole block; the roof pump runs at two because that is when there is power. Something under the dead lifts has run every night for forty years.

l_st_latch.label: A man called Latch
l_st_latch.text: A man in a clean coat brings Concern nutrient to the Stacks' trays and takes a third of the crop up the Loop; the deal has a line about who owns the deck.

l_static_forecast.label: The girl who hears
l_static_forecast.text: A girl at the Saints' tower in Bridgeward says the city's own lines in the city's own voice: names, numbers, days. What she says comes true. The Saints hear the shape of it; she hears the words.

l_bw_tenured_road.label: The near end
l_bw_tenured_road.text: House Vane holds Crown paper on the Bridgeward bridge and wants its near end for a road to the Docks by the Long Night. The Rustmouths who collect its toll are, in the Crown's words, a temporary arrangement.

l_bw_haunt.label: Back for the bridge
l_bw_haunt.text: The Rust Dogs were a crew in a Bridgeward garage before the Rustmouths took the bridge; an old Dog keeps a cache under his bench and chalks BACK FOR THE BRIDGE on the wall every spring.

l_studio_render.label: The renderer
l_studio_render.text: The Crown's studio renders portraits of people as the file expects them to become, from forecasts bought at the Exchange. The photograph is that kind of picture, made by a bigger machine than the studio's.

l_cr_concern_chair.label: The Chair is a sale
l_cr_concern_chair.text: House Vane has promised the Concern the Committee's forecasts once it holds the Chair: the Crown's futures, sold downriver before the vote.

l_cal_pencil.label: Forty-nine, in pencil
l_cal_pencil.text: On the back of the photograph, in pencil, in a hand that is not yours: 49 · VI · 12. A year, a month, a day, and no word for what the year counts from.

l_cal_year.label: Restoration Year 30
l_cal_year.text: Meridian counts its own years. The Wall says RESTORATION YEAR 30: the city's calendar starts at the Resumption, sixty years after the Burn, not at the Burn.

l_cal_r49.label: R49
l_cal_r49.text: The city's file on your face carries a date: MAGISTRATE-DESIGNATE (R49). The clerk at the gate said that was nineteen years off.

l_cal_render.label: Render 0412
l_cal_render.text: The code in the photograph's margin is a number in the city's render queue: subject, the designate; rendered R30, from forecast; depicts R49.

l_ar_steps.label: The steps
l_ar_steps.text: The broad steps at the foot of the Archive Spire are the steps in the photograph, lamp and all. The doors behind them are shut until R49.

l_ar_refusals.label: Three replies
l_ar_refusals.text: Reserve 9 has a drawer on landing ninety-one: three orders from the city to send its people to the Precinct, and three replies from MOTHER — population variance unchanged; thank you for your continuity. A fourth order is drafted.

l_ar_cast_list.label: The twelve
l_ar_cast_list.text: The list the stranger carried west is a docket under glass at the top of the Spire: twelve names, twelve places, twelve futures, in the city's even hand. Yours is the first.

l_ar_season.label: The season closes
l_ar_season.text: A hearing of the designate at the top of the Spire closes the season's accounts: every schedule on its docket is entered as final when it ends.

l_ca_chambers.label: Chambers for R49
l_ca_chambers.text: The works board on the Spire's steps: LANDING 3, COPY ROOM — MAGISTRATE'S CHAMBERS (R49). The room behind the Court is being made ready for a magistrate nineteen years early.

l_ca_petition.label: Petition 1187
l_ca_petition.text: Nobody filed the petition against the occupant of the Court's copy room. The R30 works schedule filed it, for vacant possession, and the Court has called it eleven times.

l_ca_tally.label: Asamoah, C. — Stair
l_ca_tally.text: On the Sink's tally wall: ASAMOAH, C. — R12 — STAIR, a citizen number pencilled beside it. The Sink chalked her drowned, and her number went up the stair.

l_ca_register.label: The register is a book
l_ca_register.text: The register of rulings the Court of Accounts reads from every morning is a copyist's book, slipped under the bench by the usher before the Court sits.

l_dr_card.label: A blank card
l_dr_card.text: The Crown's young people put up a purse for the final at Clover, and a Precinct citizen card with the name line blank. Whoever wins writes in it.

l_dr_fine.label: Bello's card
l_dr_fine.text: Nkechi Bello's citizen card was voided by a forecast fine, AHEAD OF PLAN, for a stall she had not opened. Her brother is still inside the Wall.

l_dr_coat.label: The Coat in the pits
l_dr_coat.text: The Crown's bookman was in the pits at night, at the Heron's back wheel, with a lamp and a little knife.

l_dr_mark.label: A ring with a bar
l_dr_mark.text: The chalk mark on Leven's door is the salvage yard's: every tower on the yard's tally that is DONE had it first. A boy is paid in water to chalk it and carry the cans.

l_dr_steel.label: Steel for the road
l_dr_steel.text: Ruben Iturbe's yard sells dead towers' steel by the ton for a road to the near end of the Bridgeward bridge, by House Vane's arrangement. A tower that burns comes down lawful.

l_hc_invitation.label: A card from Halcyon
l_hc_invitation.text: The Board of the Concern would be pleased to receive the designate at Halcyon. The Contract Office at Footgate, in the Skirts, has my name.

l_hs_geological.label: "Geological"
l_hs_geological.text: Number Six's east gallery came down on eleven miners. The Window's notice says geological, recovery not economic, and passes the dead's debts to their kin.

l_hs_log.label: The pillar log
l_hs_log.text: On the survey board in Six East, the widths of pillars fourteen to twenty-two go down week by week, four paces to one, and somebody chalked RETREAT — D. over them.

l_hs_robbed.label: Pillars cut to a waist
l_hs_robbed.text: Pillars fourteen to twenty-two in Six East were cut back to a waist with fresh pick marks: retreat mining, done with a crew still working beyond them.

l_hs_pim.label: The trapper's word
l_hs_pim.text: Pim Rasul worked the door in Six East. A man from the pit office chalked RETREAT on the pillars; the roof talked for a day; the steward said so and was told to get on.

l_hs_fall.label: Eleven lamps
l_hs_fall.text: The fall in Six East runs wall to wall. The eleven's lamps are at its edge.

l_hs_clause.label: Clause 11
l_hs_clause.text: Every miner's contract says the Concern warrants the workings: where a working fails by the Concern's order, the debts of those harmed are void and their kin compensated.

l_hs_powder.label: Six cases
l_hs_powder.text: Six cases of blasting powder are missing from Number Six's magazine. Rafe Ansel means the car's cable house.

l_hs_boots.text: Dawit Mekonnen went to the Weighhouse to clear his paper. His boots came back cleaned, with a tag in the tongue: 9-1182 — EFFECTS — RETURN TO KIN.

l_hs_book.label: The Weighhouse book
l_hs_book.text: The Weighhouse keeps a book: NAME — DEBT — YIELD — SERVICE. Yield is four letters, K L C H, graded. Service is CLINIC 9.

l_hs_yield.label: K, L, C, H
l_hs_yield.text: Kidney, liver, cornea, heart, graded for match: the Weighhouse grades debtors' organs before it sends them up for service.

l_hs_floor_nine.label: Floor nine
l_hs_floor_nine.text: Clinic service is on the Clinic floors up the hill, floor nine. Those who go up go asleep, on the freight at two.

l_hs_freight.label: The freight at two
l_hs_freight.text: At two in the morning the Clean carry sleepers on stretchers from the Weighhouse into the freight car, and a bag of effects comes down the other way.

l_hs_seal.label: The Exchange's seal
l_hs_seal.text: The changer's rate board at Two-Twelve comes up the Line every week under the Exchange's seal from Ninebridge. Six scrip to the Toll.

l_hs_par.label: Par
l_hs_par.text: The changer's ledger has a column headed PAR that never moves: the guild takes the Concern's scrip at one to one on its own floor.

l_hs_overlay.label: Deeper paper, dearer bread
l_hs_overlay.text: Provision's price board reads each customer's Window balance and moves the price a few points: the deeper the debt, the dearer the bread.

l_hs_numbed.label: Baek's arm
l_hs_numbed.text: Jun Baek's company arm goes dead to the shoulder whenever he falls behind on the Window, and wakes when he pays. Nobody touches it.

l_rc_reward.label: Two hundred for Kettle
l_rc_reward.text: The guild pays two hundred and a Line pass for the band that stops freight at Kettle Cut. A guild guard, Hamish Gorse, was killed there.

l_rc_sealed.label: Only sealed cars
l_rc_sealed.text: The cars opened at the cuttings are always the Concern's sealed ones. Nobody's purse is taken; the coach is never touched.

l_rc_manifest.label: Manifests by wire
l_rc_manifest.text: What every sealed car on the through carries goes by wire from Two-Twelve to Four Ways' signal box, and nowhere else. The band at Kettle always knows which car to open.

l_rc_stockcar.label: A stock car
l_rc_stockcar.text: One of the cars in the ditch at Kettle carried people. Its hasp was sawn from outside; inside, names scratched into the boards and a child's shoe.

l_rc_handcar.label: A handcar from the west
l_rc_handcar.text: At Kettle, in the rust on the rails, the bright line of a handcar's flanges, and hobnailed boots coming and going from the west. The band came along the track at night.

l_rc_tag.label: WH 4
l_rc_tag.text: A brass watch tag, WH 4, in the blind on the north bank at Kettle Cut.

l_rc_tagboard.label: An empty peg
l_rc_tagboard.text: West Halt's watch hangs its brass tags on a board in the watch house. The peg for number four is empty.

l_rc_casings.label: Five, then one
l_rc_casings.text: Five .308 cases where the guard stood on the coach roof at Kettle, and one 9 mm from the bank. The guard fired first.

l_rc_token.label: Occupation, permanent way
l_rc_token.text: Four Ways' register: on every night a car was opened at Kettle, the West Halt to Yard Nine section was released for OCCUPATION — PERMANENT WAY at night, by the stationmaster's own release, C.B.

l_rc_wires.label: Ticks on the wire
l_rc_wires.text: The stationmaster copies the through's manifests off the wire, and ticks some of the sealed cars in pencil.

l_rc_tins.label: Concern tins, cheap
l_rc_tins.text: The halts' stalls sell Concern tins at two Tolls, a third of the price anywhere else, and nobody says where from.

l_rc_length.label: Length money
l_rc_length.text: The guild pays the halts length money for keeping their track, but per train that stops. Since through-running, nothing stops, and nothing is paid.

l_rc_tower.label: The tower at West Halt
l_rc_tower.text: West Halt's water tower is padlocked with the ladder drawn up, and people are living in it.

l_rc_intake.label: Intake
l_rc_intake.text: The twelve in West Halt's tower are on Concern paper from the Ninebridge block: INTAKE — WEIGHHOUSE — TWO-TWELVE.

l_rc_asleep.label: Dorcas asleep
l_rc_asleep.text: Dorcas's controller is not burned. It is a Concern board, the closed eye on it, with one lamp blinking a pattern, waiting for something.

l_rc_timing.label: The night after
l_rc_timing.text: Dorcas died the night after Ida Szalai sent the Concern's first letter back unsigned.

l_rc_spanner.label: Bright threads
l_rc_spanner.text: East Halt's long track spanner hangs in the tool shed with fresh oil on it, and the bolts on the east length have bright threads where they were backed off.

l_rc_kofi.label: Out at night
l_rc_kofi.text: Kofi Mensah counts the through's cars every night, and lately he has seen the halt's keeper out on the east length with a lamp after dark.

l_ds_sheen.label: The sheen
l_ds_sheen.text: Since the thaw Gull Stilts' water has a skin on it like a bruise, purple and gold, thickest toward the east. The fish taste of it.

l_ds_kai.label: Kai Tanoa
l_ds_kai.text: Kai Tanoa, eleven, dove under the Gut by the third pile from the Greta to free his mother's net, in black water, and did not come up.

l_ds_joint.label: Joint fourteen
l_ds_joint.text: The old export line from the Rigs runs along the bottom under the Gut to Blackcap. Its joint fourteen has split and breathes crude. Kai's net was caught on its collar.

l_ds_blackcap.label: Blackcap
l_ds_blackcap.text: The drowned terminal's last tank, full to the brim, with a new guild pump on its rim and the water round it black.

l_ds_barge.label: The night barge
l_ds_barge.text: A guild barge loads at Blackcap at night with no lamps, three nights in four, and goes up the delta low in the water.

l_ds_pressure.label: Eleven points
l_ds_pressure.text: Hum's export pressure has fallen eleven points since the thaw. Hamid Farouk says Hum is tired. His daughter says something is drinking.

l_ds_seal.label: LINE ACCOUNT
l_ds_seal.text: A fresh lead seal on Hum's export valve under the sea: TOLLMEN — LINE ACCOUNT. The guild seals what it means to bill.

l_ds_two_tankers.label: Two for one
l_ds_two_tankers.text: The tide post's day-book: two loads a month off Blackcap entered to the Line's fuel book, one tanker a month paid to Hum, and a column headed SHRINKAGE.

l_ds_tide_table.label: Never wrong yet
l_ds_tide_table.text: The tide table at Gull Stilts' Landing is printed by the Precinct, two low waters a day to the minute. Someone has pencilled under it: NEVER WRONG YET.

l_ds_brand.label: N-B 4471
l_ds_brand.text: Mateo Ibarra's wrist carries a Ninebridge block brand, N-B 4471, two years healed. He was sold, not drowned.

l_ds_curlew_adrift.label: Oars shipped
l_ds_curlew_adrift.text: Mele Tui found the Curlew adrift off the Jesty with her oars shipped and lashed and Mateo's coat folded in the bow. A drowning man does neither.

l_ds_finders_fee.label: Finder's fee
l_ds_finders_fee.text: The guild's collections: IBARRA, M. — TAKEN AT THE GUT, NIGHT — GIVEN BY J. SOUSA — FINDER'S FEE: HIS BOAT. VESSEL SET ADRIFT, COAT ABOARD.

l_ds_wrecks.label: Five barges
l_ds_wrecks.text: The Book of Water: five guild barges wrecked on the Jesty since the fish went black, and none in the eleven years before while Lean's light burned.

l_ds_lamp_cut.label: Lean's lamp
l_ds_lamp_cut.text: Lean's light has been dark on five foggy nights since the thaw: its gas line cut clean with a knife each time, and spliced each morning.

l_ds_soot.label: Soot on the Jesty
l_ds_soot.text: A new iron hook on the Jesty's seaward parapet, and a fan of lamp soot above it on the concrete.

l_ds_roof_lamp.label: A lamp on the roofs
l_ds_roof_lamp.text: From the dike at night, in fog, a lamp moving low over the drowned roofs off Gull Stilts, where nobody lives.

l_dk_box.label: Thirty-one on fourteen
l_dk_box.text: The box that fell from Crane Six is stencilled MACHINE PARTS — 14 T under a whole Concern seal. Through the split: cast copper ingots, thirty tonnes of them if it is one.

l_dk_tape.label: Key 6/N
l_dk_tape.text: Crane Six's load tape: a lift of 31.2 tonnes at six past two, the overload cutout tripped, then overridden a minute later with the night key, 6/N. At ten past, the spreader's lock let go.

l_dk_key.label: A key cut by hand
l_dk_key.text: Dmytro Lysenko kept a crane key cut by hand from a blank, stamped 6/N, in a tin on his shelf, with a Bond night pass marked D.L.

l_dk_medicine.label: Blue caps
l_dk_medicine.text: In the same tin: two blue-capped Concern inhalers, the medicine his daughter breathes through, that no docker's tallies could buy.

l_dk_slip.label: Two weights
l_dk_slip.text: The Concern's own loading slip says the box was 31.4 tonnes of copper. The guild's freight bill for the same seal says 14 tonnes of machine parts.

l_dk_unweighed.label: NOT WEIGHED
l_dk_unweighed.text: The weighbridge register: every box off the through for two years, NOT WEIGHED — THROUGH PATH, by order. The guild bills its freight by the ton.

l_dk_short.label: Five on eight
l_dk_short.text: Gang Nine worked Crane Six five hands where the crane's complement is eight, by the Harbour Master's order, to turn the through in the four hours its contract allows.

l_dk_returnable.label: A returnable lost
l_dk_returnable.text: The Bond's notice on the guild floor's door: RETURNABLE LOST FROM BOND — ONE — REWARD 60 — APPLY THE BOND OFFICER.

l_dk_surety.label: Surety
l_dk_surety.text: Mirela Stan, fifteen, is the surety on her mother's Concern contract in the Skirts: returnable on default or flight. Her flight is the default.

l_dk_lease.label: The berths leased
l_dk_lease.text: The Harbour Master has leased the river berths under the Hulls to House Vane for works. The occupiers are to quit on the commencement of works.

l_dk_act.label: Schedule three
l_dk_act.text: The Harbour Act, Schedule 3: a vessel in port shall not be moved, broken or removed while she has a crew aboard, save by her master's leave or the court's order on proof of abandonment.

l_dk_crews.label: Crew books
l_dk_crews.text: Every hull on the dry bed has a master and a crew book, and the crews have signed them every Sunday for ninety years.

l_dk_signed.label: Three marks
l_dk_signed.text: Three of the nine hulls' masters have put their marks to House Vane's papers of abandonment, at forty Tolls a hull.

l_dk_footing.label: A second footing
l_dk_footing.text: The pre-war survey plate on the river wall shows the old tram bridge's footing a hundred and twenty metres downstream: sound rock, under the edge of the Concern's Bond.

l_tm_taken.label: Taken on the path
l_tm_taken.text: Three names chalked under a line on Number Four's lamp board this year: runaways from the Skirts taken by the Clean at the switchback below the col, before they reached the pit.

l_tm_cut.label: Nothing to track
l_tm_cut.text: Four's cutter took the Concern's chrome out of all three of the taken, weeks before. Nothing in them could have told the Clean where they were.

l_tm_waiting.label: Told the hour
l_tm_waiting.text: The Clean were at the switchback on the col at dawn before the last taking, waiting, with no lamp: men who had been told the hour.

l_tm_radio.label: VISITORS
l_tm_radio.text: The winding house's old field set, and its log in the winchwoman's hand: FOUR — CLEAR — SNOW ON THE COL every dawn, and on three nights this year, the nights before the takings, VISITORS.

l_tm_price.label: Double for tin
l_tm_price.text: The guild's buyer at East Halt pays twelve a bar for Number Four's tin. Ninebridge pays six. Nobody pays double for tin.

l_tm_requests.label: The requests card
l_tm_requests.text: A Concern card in the winchwoman's locker: a name a season for fifteen winters, a letter or two after each name, and this season's line a woman's name. FOUR — ARRANGEMENT — RENEWED.

l_tm_yield.label: The Weighhouse's letters
l_tm_yield.text: The letters after the names on the card are the Weighhouse's yield grades: kidney, liver, cornea, heart. Four's cutter wrote them herself for nine years.

l_tm_digger.label: The digger
l_tm_digger.text: In the old level under Number Four, a pre-war mining machine with the Concern's closed eye on it lies where it stopped, and its lamp has started blinking since the water went off it.

l_nw_short.label: Eleven seasons short
l_nw_short.text: The city's notice: Ashby has delivered short of its schedule for eleven seasons, and an inspector is coming up the river to read the gauge.

l_nw_gauge.label: The sixth mark
l_nw_gauge.text: The staff gauge painted on Ashby's upstream face shows the Water at the sixth mark of ten. The controller in the gatehouse reads it full.

l_nw_jam.label: A block in the well
l_nw_jam.text: In the gauge-well hut on Ashby's crest, the float that tells the controller how full the Water is has been wedged at the top of its well with an oak block, old and black with handling.

l_nw_crack.label: The pins
l_nw_crack.text: In the gallery inside the dam, a crack runs down the west wall, pinned and chalked with sixty years of dates. It has opened a finger's width in that time, a little more every wet season.

l_nw_keepers_log.label: Never above the sixth
l_nw_keepers_log.text: The keepers' own log, Year 60, in Hedda Wexford's grandmother's hand: NEVER ABOVE THE SIXTH MARK. SHE WILL NOT HOLD IT.

l_nw_clause31.label: Shortfall from the Sink
l_nw_clause31.text: The footnote on Ashby's schedule card: SPRING RELIEF TO PRECINCT SUPPLY (CL. 31, GROWTH) — SHORTFALL MET FROM SINK RELIEF. When Ashby comes in short, the city takes the Sink's pumps.

l_nw_warranty.label: The lessor warrants the works
l_nw_warranty.text: Ashby's lease, framed in the gatehouse: the Water is the city's for a hundred and fifty years, and in its eleventh clause the Ashby trust, whose heirs are a house of the Crown, warrants the works for the term.

l_nw_marks.label: Marks cut over
l_nw_marks.text: In Sawtown's north pen: the Ridge's crow's feet shaved off logs' butts and the Bottoms' hook cut over the place with a scribe. The boom paid the Bottoms for them.

l_nw_punt.label: A lamp at the north pen
l_nw_punt.text: At night a punt with a shuttered lamp goes out to the north pen and a girl in it cuts marks: Sigrun Brandvold, the Ridge foreman's own daughter.

l_nw_tally.label: Half again
l_nw_tally.text: The boom's tally: the Bottoms have been paid this season for half again what four saws on the flats can fell.

l_nw_baby.label: A woman's board
l_nw_baby.text: Rufino Huaman of the Bottoms pays Dorit at the cookhouse for a woman's board: his daughter Wayra, and her baby, whom the Ridge will not look at.

l_nw_stump.label: A barber chair
l_nw_stump.text: The stump where Mikkel Brandvold died: cut from the Ridge's own side, the back-cut too low, the trunk split up the middle as it went. A tree felled in a hurry, in the wet, by somebody told to fell it.

l_nw_order.label: Up in the rain
l_nw_order.text: Arvid Brandvold sent his son up to fell the big leaner on the boundary in the rain, the morning before the Bottoms meant to cut it, so the Ridge would have it first.

l_nw_crates.label: KENNEL
l_nw_crates.text: The Patience's sealed cases: boards potted in black resin with the Concern's closed eye, each in straw, each tagged KENNEL and a number, each with a socket shaped for something's neck.

l_nw_kennel.label: Dogs' brains
l_nw_kennel.text: The reed people of the river know a kennel board when they see one: a controller for a hound, a machine dog. Somebody means to wake dogs in the city.
